title: Separation of powers and checks & balances
quote: Constitutional government = limited government: it defines, restrains and checks power

boxes.title: Core ideas
items: **Constitutional government** = ==**limited government**==, limited by the terms of the Constitution (UPSC 2020, 2021)
Best safeguard of liberty in a liberal democracy: ==**separation of powers**== (UPSC 2021)
**Montesquieu**: "**The Spirit of Laws**" (**1748**); drew on the British constitution
**Constitutionalism**: limits + rule of law + checks & balances + judicial review + FRs
**PIL**: strengthens access to justice but **not indispensable** for Rule of Law (Arts. **14, 32, 226**)
**Ambedkar**: preferred **responsibility over stability**

boxes.title: Degree in India
items: ==**No rigid separation**==; implicit, not absolute; overlapping functions
Parliamentary = **fusion**: executive drawn from and accountable to legislature
Nominal head (**President**) vs real head (**Council of Ministers**)
**Art. 50 (DPSP)**: separate judiciary from executive
Judiciary insulated: Arts. **50, 121, 211, 235**

boxes.title: Judicial checks
items: **Judicial review**: Arts. **13, 32, 226**; ultra vires laws void
==**Art. 121 / 211**==: Parliament / State Legislature cannot discuss conduct of SC/HC judge (except removal motion)
**Art. 122 / 212**: courts cannot question legislative procedure
**Art. 142** complete justice: Vishaka before **POSH Act, 2013**; risk of overreach

boxes.title: Landmark cases
head: Case
Holding
rows: Legislature cannot decide election dispute; **39th Amdt** validation struck
Ninth Schedule entries post-**24 Apr 1973** reviewable

boxes.title: Exam corner
items: In India ==**executive is subordinate to legislature**== (BPSC 2001)
**121/211** = legislature can't discuss judges; **122/212** = courts can't question procedure
"Parliament can overrule a judgment by simple resolution" = **false**
**One Nation One Election** Bill amends Arts. **83, 172, 327**; AP: Madras Presidency separated Collector's judicial powers in **1816**
